It even specifies the M4 obligation ("delete one §9 limit ... and the named row must fail"). The gap is self-declared by the spec, not an over-reading by the reviewer. Commit 4afdf2b shipped the two .md files and nothing else.

Route 3 — "something else enforces it indirectly." Nothing does. A targeted grep across every .ts, .py, .sh and .json in the repo finds the two doc paths only in docs/build spec/state JSON and in scripts/verify-acceptance.sh. No product source reads them either, so no test can assert on them transitively, and no test globs conductor/docs.

Route 4 — "the scenario cannot actually occur / the code handles it." It occurs. I ran the exact row 11a/11b logic against mutated copies: OPERATIONS.md reduced from 293 lines to a single heading still prints PASS row 11a, and limit 7 inverted from a disclosure of a real weakness into a false reassurance still prints PASS row 11b, because the count of `^[0-9]+\. \*\*` lines is unchanged at 15. The 1280-test suite is provably untouched by the mutation since nothing in it reads the files, and the baseline gate is green (1280/1280 GATE PASS), so the mutated tree would report the same green.

The one nuance worth handing to the orchestrator, and it does not rescue the code: row 11b is not literally zero-signal. Deleting a limit outright drops the count to 14 and fails the row. What it cannot see is any edit that preserves the number of list items — rewriting, inverting, or hollowing out a limit's body — and it has no visibility at all into OPERATIONS.md beyond existence. The finding's wording, "Neither reads a word of either file," is accurate: a count of line prefixes is not a content check, and the failure mode the finding picks (rewrite, not delete) sits squarely in the blind spot.

Two trivial citation slips, neither affecting the verdict: the row-11 block starts at line 237 (the OPS/LIM assignments), not 239; and the finding's `find conductor/tests -name ops-docs.test.ts` phrasing is confirmed empty but the tree does contain a similarly-named doctrine.test.ts that is unrelated. Severity MAJOR is right — this is the only mechanical enforcement the two docs were ever going to get, and it is absent, leaving 25 assertion rows resting on a file-exists check and a list-item tally.

*Skeptic 2 (could not refute):* The finding holds exactly as stated; I tried to break it four ways and each attempt confirmed it.

(1) The spec's own specGaps field names the missing artifact verbatim: "the task ships THREE files — conductor/tests/ops-docs.test.ts (written FIRST, red by construction), conductor/docs/OPERATIONS.md and conductor/docs/HONEST-LIMITS.md". `ls conductor/tests/` lists 56 files; neither ops-docs.test.ts nor docs.test.ts is among them. `git show --stat 4afdf2b` shows exactly two files changed (HONEST-LIMITS.md +80, OPERATIONS.md +293) and STATE.json's 15.1 filesTouched lists those same two.
